dialogue.chat: The door said you'd come. The door is never wrong twice. Speak, %1$s.
dialogue.chat/1: The bucket said you'd stop by, and the bucket keeps good time. Speak, I'm listening — so is the bucket.
dialogue.chat/2: Ah, you. The candles flickered a welcome. Sit where the floor doesn't creak accusingly, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations: You want to talk? The fence and I just finished. Your timing is excellent. Ask anything — I've already told the bucket.
dialogue.conversations/1: Talk! Yes. I've warmed up on the bucket, so my words are the right temperature now. Go on, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations/2: The spoons rearranged themselves into a listening shape this morning. They knew. Ask away.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.good: The bees hummed in E this week, which means luck. Also I found my other spoon. So: thriving, thank you for asking.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.good/1: Good — the moths flew clockwise, which is the lucky direction. Also I have both socks. A rich week.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.good/2: Thriving. The well echoed twice this morning, and two is the number for yes. I trust the well, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.rough: The door has been sticking, and doors know things. It's been a heavy week, %1$s. The door agrees with me.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.rough/1: The hinges have been sighing, and hinges are honest. A heavy week. Even the cat's been philosophical.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.again: You've asked before — the bucket remembers. The answer hasn't changed shape yet, %1$s. These things ripen slowly.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.again/1: Twice! The candles noticed too. Still the same, still glad you count. The floorboards are warming to you.
dialogue.conversations.day.good: A seventeen-cloud day. Those are the good ones. I told the well this morning and it echoed back, which is a yes.
dialogue.conversations.day.good/1: A twelve-bird morning and a cloud shaped like forgiveness. The signs are all pointing gentle today.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough: The bread came out shaped like the mayor. I ate it anyway, but we were both uncomfortable about it.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough/1: The porridge whispered something rude and I've been off-balance since. Some days start on the wrong omen, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.work.like: The work likes me, which matters more. Tools remember gentle hands. Mine remember me back — except the hammer. We're quarreling.
dialogue.conversations.work.like/1: The tools and I have an understanding. All but the hammer — we're in a silent feud, and I intend to win it.
dialogue.conversations.work.hate: I asked my boots whether I like the job. They said we walk there slower every year. Boots can't lie. No mouths.
dialogue.conversations.work.hate/1: My boots say we go slower each year, and boots don't lie — no mouths to lie WITH. So: mixed feelings.
dialogue.conversations.village.home: %2$s sits at exactly the right angle to the sunset, which is why the bread rises here and nowhere else. Home, obviously.
dialogue.conversations.village.home/1: I know which stones in %2$s are listening and which are just resting. It's a good village. The well vouches for it.
dialogue.conversations.people.first: Good folk. I've assigned each of them a cloud. The mayor's is stubborn; the baker's is warm. It's a whole system, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.people.first/1: The neighbors are lovely once you learn their weathers. Some are drizzle, some are noon. All are welcome at my fence.
dialogue.conversations.food.first: Whatever the bucket recommends. Today it said turnips, but the bucket has an agenda. I'm having bread instead.
dialogue.conversations.food.first/1: Soup, if it's the right shape in the bowl. Round is calm, oval is ambitious. I eat by the omens, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.life.first: Born on a Tuesday, which explains a lot. A flood, a goose I still owe an apology, one summer I keep in a jar. I'll start with the goose.
dialogue.conversations.life.first/1: It began on a Tuesday and never fully recovered. There's a goose I wronged and a summer in a jar. Where to start...
dialogue.conversations.dreams.first: I dream of a staircase that goes sideways, into a room where everyone I ever fed is fine. The chickens agree it's real.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.first/1: A sideways staircase to a warm room where everyone I ever fed is safe. The chickens have confirmed it's real.
dialogue.conversations.fears.first: The gap between thunder and thunder — that's when the sky decides. And that only the bucket would miss me. ...Silly. Probably.
dialogue.conversations.fears.first/1: The silence between two thunderclaps — that's when the sky is deciding. And being missed only by the bucket.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.first: The candles burn straighter when you're here, %1$s. I checked three times. You make the room make sense. Don't tell the candles.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.first/1: You arrive and the candles stand up straighter. I've measured it, %1$s. You make the room agree with itself.
dialogue.conversations.deflect.personal: That answer lives under the third floorboard, and the floorboard doesn't know you yet. Come by more. Floorboards warm up. So do I.
dialogue.conversations.deflect.personal/: That's under the third floorboard, and it hasn't met you yet. Visit more. Floorboards warm slowly. So do I.
dialogue.conversations.deflect.intimate: That one I've only ever told the well, and the well earned it over years. Keep coming around, %1$s. You're getting well-shaped.
dialogue.conversations.deflect.intimate/: Only the well knows that one, and it took years to earn it. Keep coming round — you're getting well-shaped, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.none: The weathervane hasn't moved in three days, which is either no news or very big news. I'm treating it as no news. Safer.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.none/1: The weathervane's held still three days. Either nothing's happening or everything is. I've chosen to believe nothing. Calmer.
dialogue.conversations.us.happy.yes: Happy? The candles burn straight, the well says yes twice, and my odd little world makes sense with you in it. So: yes.
dialogue.conversations.us.happy.yes/1: You're the one thing the omens and I agree on completely, %1$s. That's never happened before. Yes. Yes.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.marriage: %2$s and %3$s got married, and the bells rang in a key I'd never heard before — a good key, the well confirmed it.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.marriage/1: %2$s wed %3$s under a cloud shaped like a knot, which is the marrying cloud. The bucket wept, happily I think.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.divorce: %2$s and %3$s parted ways. The weathervane spun twice and stopped facing nowhere in particular. These things happen.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.divorce/1: %2$s and %3$s aren't together anymore. Two spoons that used to nest now sit apart in my drawer. They knew before I did.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.death: %2$s has passed on, %1$s. The candles all leaned toward their house last night, saying goodbye in the only way candles can.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.death/1: We lost %2$s. The well echoed once this morning, and one is the number for farewell. I'll miss them terribly.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.birth: A baby! %2$s brought a new little one into the world, and the chickens have been clucking lullabies all day.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.birth/1: %2$s had a baby, %1$s! I've already assigned the child a cloud — a soft, round, brand-new one. Welcome, little cloud.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.arrival: %2$s has moved into the village. The floorboards by their new door are still learning their footsteps, but they'll warm up.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.arrival/1: Someone new — %2$s! The fence introduced us. I've decided they're a noon sort of person, which is a fine sort to be.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.departure: %2$s packed up and left for good. Their empty chair is holding their shape for now; chairs are loyal like that.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.departure/: %2$s has gone away, %1$s. I keep setting out one too many turnips. The habit hasn't heard the news yet.
